newsitem.title: UK: Britain diplomatic on ASEAN admission of Burma.
newsitem.headline: Britain diplomatic on ASEAN admission of Burma.

text.p: Britain on Saturday steered clear of entering a diplomatic row over the decision by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to admit Burma as a member in defiance of international pressure.
The Foreign Office said in a short statement that "the question of membership of ASEAN is a matter for member states."
"The essential thing is that the whole international community should make clear to Burma the need for democratic reform and the restoration of human rights," the statement added.

ASEAN decided on Saturday to admit Burma, Cambodia and Laos as its last three members in July. But the group, founded in 1967 as an anti-Communist bulwark, had been under international pressure to defer Burma's admission over its human rights record.

Britain last week called in Burma's ambassador to London to protest over the recent arrest of some 100 members of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy before a party gathering.
